message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to want to back out of the promise I made to my wife after the affair. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I cheated on my wife, which is a huge mistake. I've already owned up to that, and that's not what this is about. My wife gave me a chance to make things right by agreeing to stay with me if I made the next year all about her. I agreed because I thought it meant doing things like massages, shopping, and her favorite things. But instead, she decided the year would be all about Disney. Now, I'm a bit confused because I didn't realize she was so into Disney. Our daughters loved it when they were little, but they're grown up now. I thought her interest was mostly for the kids. But she's made me go to Disneyland seven times this year and Harry Potter World once. I guess that was okay, but the costs add up. She even made me cosplay as Disney characters, including a Beauty and the Beast costume that cost $800. Plus, she makes me watch Frozen every day, and when I asked to change it, she put on Pocahontas 2. I know this isn't as bad as the cheating, but I'm really miserable. I can't keep doing this. I want to have an intervention where we stop all the Disney stuff and just go to counseling, which should have happened a while ago. Is it AITA (a**hole in the afternoon) for me to want to back out? Hmm, so I need to think about whether wanting to break this promise is right or wrong. Let me break it down. First, I made a promise to my wife to make the year about her as part of the healing process after the affair. She chose Disney, which I didn't expect. I went along with it, but it's causing me a lot of stress and unhappiness. I feel like it's not helping our relationship and that we should focus on counseling instead. On one hand, I kept my promise by agreeing to make the year about her, but the way she's interpreting it is causing me distress. On the other hand, I'm feeling like I'm being taken advantage of, and my needs aren't being considered. I want to prioritize counseling because that's what I think we both need to work through the issues caused by the affair. I wonder if it's fair to her to change the terms of the agreement. She might feel like I'm not keeping my word, which could hurt her trust in me again. But I'm also feeling like I'm being forced into something that's not healthy for me, which is affecting our relationship negatively. Maybe I should consider talking to her about how I'm feeling instead of planning an intervention. If I approach her calmly and express that I'm struggling with the Disney focus and that I think counseling would be more beneficial, she might understand. It's possible that she's using Disney as a way to cope with her pain, and I need to respect that while also taking care of my own emotional well-being. I also need to think about the long-term health of our relationship. If we're not addressing the underlying issues through counseling, we might be setting ourselves up for more problems down the line. But I also don't want to come across as dismissive of her needs or as someone who doesn't keep his promises. Perhaps a compromise could be reached where we continue some Disney activities but also start attending counseling sessions. That way, both of our needs are addressed, and we can work on healing together. It's important to communicate openly and find a middle ground that respects both of our feelings and needs. In the end, I don't want to be seen as breaking a promise, but I also don't want to continue in a situation that's making me miserable and not helping our relationship. It's a tough spot, and I need to approach it with empathy and understanding for both myself and my wife.
